title: Gogo Sorghum and Groundnut Paste
localName: Ugali wa Mtama na Karanga — Wagogo
community: Gogo people of Dodoma — the dry plateau people
author: Mama Salima

heritage.origin: Gogo people of the Dodoma plateau — the dry heartland of Tanzania
heritage.history: The Gogo (Wagogo) people inhabit the central plateau of Tanzania around Dodoma — one of the driest, most challenging environments in the country. Their ecology has shaped a cuisine built around extreme drought resilience: sorghum, finger millet, groundnuts, and cattle. The Gogo are also renowned across Tanzania for their music — the traditional tunes (nyimbo za Wagogo) are among the country's most distinctive. Gogo food reflects their environment: simple, nourishing, and built to sustain people through drought. The combination of sorghum ugali with thick groundnut sauce is the Gogo's most fundamental meal.

desc: Gogo Sorghum Ugali with Groundnut Sauce — stiff sorghum porridge served with a thick peanut sauce made from roasted groundnuts, tomatoes, and onions. The foundational meal of Tanzania's dry plateau — two drought-resistant crops combined into a complete, nourishing dish.
longDesc: The Gogo meal is the definition of resourcefulness — sorghum ugali and groundnut sauce require no animal products, use only drought-resistant crops, and together provide a nutritionally complete meal. The groundnut sauce (made by roasting and grinding local groundnuts with tomato and onion) is richer and more complex than peanut butter, producing a dish of genuine depth.
ingredients: 1 cup raw groundnuts — roasted and ground coarsely
steps: Make groundnut sauce: roast groundnuts in dry pan until golden. Cool. Grind coarsely.
Heat oil. Cook onions until golden. Add tomatoes. Cook 5 minutes.
Mix ground groundnuts with ½ cup warm water to a paste. Add to tomato base.
Add remaining water. Simmer 12—15 minutes until thick. Season.
Serve ugali with groundnut sauce alongside.
chefTips: Roasting the groundnuts fresh produces far more flavour than using commercial peanut butter.
The sauce should be thick enough to eat with ugali — not pourable.
commonMistakes: Using commercial peanut butter instead of fresh-roasted — different character entirely.
cookingScience: See TZA049 for groundnut sauce science. Freshly roasted and ground groundnuts contain more volatile aromatic compounds (pyrazines from roasting) than commercial peanut butter — producing a more complex, nutty sauce.
sustainabilityTips: Both sorghum and groundnuts are nitrogen-fixing or drought-resistant — the most climate-resilient possible meal.
servedWith: As a complete meal — this is the Gogo daily plate
reheating: Gently with a splash of water.
healthBenefits: Sorghum provides complex carbohydrate and antioxidants.
Groundnuts provide complete protein and healthy fats.
Together: a complete, balanced meal from drought-resistant crops.
culturalNote: The Gogo sorghum-groundnut meal is the food of Tanzania's driest heartland — the meal that sustains a people through drought, through hardship, and through the remarkable cultural richness (especially in music) that the Wagogo have always maintained regardless of environmental conditions.
